sub_area: concurrent_limit decorator — Redis-backed per-function semaphore, 503 on exhaustion, token release on success/exception, self-heal after TTL expiry, fail-open when Redis down
rationale: Tests the Python concurrent_limit decorator and its interaction with frappe.cache (Redis) entirely in-process; ferro has no equivalent concurrency-limiter middleware and intentionally does not reimplement this Python subsystem.

sub_area: get_modules_from_all_apps_for_user — module list derivation from Module Def doctype
rationale: Calls the Python utility get_modules_from_all_apps_for_user() in-process; ferro does not expose a module-list endpoint and this is a Desk boot helper, not a REST API ferro reimplements.

sub_area: CORS response headers — Access-Control-Allow-Origin/Methods/Headers/Credentials/Vary based on allow_cors config
rationale: Tests that the CORS headers are correctly added/suppressed based on site config; ferro's HTTP server must also emit correct CORS headers for cross-origin Desk/SPA clients, so the behavior is in scope, but the tests drive Frappe's WSGI stack in-process rather than hitting ferro over HTTP.

sub_area: frappe.desk.notifications.get_open_count — internal/external link counts on Desk dashboard connections panel
rationale: Exercises the Desk dashboard connections Python logic (get_open_count) entirely in-process; ferro does not reimplement this Desk-specific helper and it is not part of the core REST/ORM contract.

sub_area: frappe.db Python ORM — get_value/get_values, set_value, exists, count, bulk_insert, transaction writes, read-only mode, datetime serialization, savepoint
rationale: Tests Frappe's Python database layer (frappe.db.*) directly in-process; ferro reimplements the same SQLite read/write semantics in orm.rs but uses its own Rust code path — these tests encode the ORM contract ferro must match (filters, set_value semantics, bulk_insert) even though they do not exercise ferro over HTTP.

sub_area: MariaDB DDL — rename_table, describe, change_column_type, add_index
rationale: MariaDB-only DDL operations (RENAME TABLE, CHANGE COLUMN TYPE) are irrelevant to ferro which targets SQLite; ferro's schema.rs handles DDL separately and does not replicate Python-side MariaDB DDL helpers.

sub_area: frappe.db.set_value — single/multi-row updates, update_modified options, single doctype field updates
rationale: Tests the in-process set_value/get_value contract which maps to ferro's orm.rs update path; ferro must produce equivalent behavior for ORM writes over HTTP, but these tests never call ferro directly.

sub_area: PostgreSQL DDL — rename, describe, change_column_type, add_index, unique constraints
rationale: PostgreSQL-specific DDL tests; ferro targets SQLite and does not reimplement Postgres DDL helpers.

sub_area: PostgreSQL transaction ID consistency across commit/rollback
rationale: PostgreSQL-specific transaction ID test using txid_current(); ferro uses SQLite and handles transactions natively in Rust, making this test irrelevant.

sub_area: Read replica connection switching via frappe.read_only() decorator
rationale: Tests Python-level read-replica connection management; ferro does not implement read-replica routing and this is a Python framework internal unrelated to ferro's REST surface.

sub_area: SQLite/DB row-level locking — skip_locked, no-wait, delete race condition, value cache invalidation
rationale: Tests frappe.db-level locking primitives (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, NOWAIT) via Python ORM using dual connections; ferro manages its own SQLite concurrency in Rust and these Python-DB-layer locking tests do not exercise it.

sub_area: frappe.db.sql iterator/cursor modes — as_iterator, pluck, unbuffered cursor
rationale: Tests Python-level SQL iterator and unbuffered cursor abstractions that are internal to frappe.db; ferro uses its own Rust SQLite driver and does not expose these Python cursor concepts.

sub_area: PostgreSQL multi-schema isolation — table/column introspection scoped to correct schema
rationale: PostgreSQL-only multi-schema tests; ferro targets SQLite which has no schema isolation concept.

sub_area: frappe.db.connect() environment-variable credential override (DB_NAME/HOST/USER/PASSWORD/PORT)
rationale: Tests Python frappe.db.connect() credential handling via environment variables; ferro reads its own site_config.json for DB path and has no equivalent credential-override mechanism to test.

sub_area: MariaDB exception utility methods — is_deadlocked/timedout/table_missing etc. with empty args
rationale: MariaDB-specific exception utility methods; ferro uses SQLite and maps errors in Rust without this Python utility layer.

sub_area: DatabaseQuery / frappe.get_all — filters, child table joins, permission-masking, permlevel fields, user permissions, date filters, order_by, distinct, ignore_permissions
rationale: Tests the full DatabaseQuery filter/permission logic that ferro's orm.rs must replicate exactly for get_list; ferro's build_list_query implements the same filter operators, perm-level masking, and user-permission scoping that this test class encodes.

sub_area: frappe.desk.reportview — get_count, get with field/permlevel filters, child table filter, distinct
rationale: Tests reportview.get_count and reportview.get which ferro exposes via desk.rs (frappe.desk.reportview.*); ferro must produce the same count/filter semantics, though the tests drive the Python handler in-process rather than over HTTP.

sub_area: frappe.db.updatedb — DDL sync from DocType definition (column types, defaults, indexes, unique constraints, bigint/UUID migration)
rationale: Tests the Python DDL migration logic (updatedb) that maps DocType field definitions to SQL column types; ferro's schema.rs implements an equivalent mapping for SQLite install/migrate, so the type-mapping semantics are relevant even though the tests are in-process Python.

sub_area: No-op migrate check — ensure repeated reload_doctype does not emit unnecessary ALTER statements
rationale: SQLite-skipped test verifying Python's idempotent DDL migration; ferro's schema.rs has its own md5-gated idempotent sync and this specific Python-level ALTER suppression test does not apply to ferro.

sub_area: frappe.defaults — global/user defaults set/get/add/clear, user-permission filtering of defaults
rationale: Tests the Python defaults system (tabDefaultValue) which is a Frappe framework internal used by the Desk; ferro does not reimplement defaults management and it is not part of the REST API ferro exposes.

sub_area: deferred_insert — cache-buffered batch insert flushed to DB via save_to_db
rationale: Tests the deferred insert mechanism that buffers route history writes via cache before flushing; ferro does not reimplement deferred insert and this is a Python background-job pattern.

sub_area: DocStatus enum — is_draft/is_submitted/is_cancelled predicate methods
rationale: Tests a pure Python IntEnum utility class with no HTTP surface; ferro stores docstatus as an integer field and does not need to reimplement this enum's predicate methods.

sub_area: Document insert/update/delete/load, naming, child tables, hooks, version tracking, submission workflow, validation
rationale: Tests the Python Document class lifecycle (insert, save, submit, cancel, naming, child-table handling, hooks); ferro's orm.rs covers the insert/update/read data path but not Python-side hooks, validation, or WebsiteGenerator — the ORM contract behaviors (naming, child tables) are relevant to ferro even though tests are in-process.

sub_area: WebsiteGenerator web view — Document Share Key auth, GET /ToDo/<name>?key=, 403/410 responses
rationale: Tests Frappe's website generator web-view rendering with document share keys via Python WSGI stack; ferro does not implement the website generator or share-key authentication for HTML views.

sub_area: frappe.get_lazy_doc — deferred child-table fetch, query-count efficiency, db_update_all
rationale: Tests the Python LazyDocument descriptor and deferred child-table loading optimization; ferro always fetches child tables eagerly in orm.rs and does not implement lazy document loading.

sub_area: frappe.get_docs — bulk document retrieval with child tables, filters, limit, order_by, as_iterator
rationale: Tests frappe.get_docs bulk retrieval which parallels ferro's get_list + per-doc child-table fetch; the filter/limit/order_by semantics are relevant to ferro's orm.rs but get_docs is a Python-only API not directly exposed by ferro's HTTP routes.

sub_area: DocsCollection descriptor — typed doctype-scoped helpers (.docs.get/.new/.last/.filter/.delete) on Document subclasses
rationale: Tests a Python-only controller-class descriptor API (DocsCollection) that is syntactic sugar over frappe.get_doc/get_list; ferro has no equivalent typed-descriptor concept and this is purely a Python framework convenience.

sub_area: Document locking — lock/unlock, DocumentLockedError on concurrent lock, auto-expiry after N days
rationale: Tests the Python document-locking mechanism (stored in tabCommunication/cache); ferro does not implement document locks and the REST API ferro exposes does not include a locking endpoint.
